# Performance AFTER-deploy receipt: pr:310

Deployed merge: fb565c165d74a3715ac5c24f477fa5496bef7e4b. Reviewed head: 7f83e0defd62fb5da0170b02afb6af4872ccbaa3. Live daemon: PID 31125, ping commit fb565c165d, process start November 21, 2026, 06:06:56 UTC. No bounce, restart, competing receiver or product edit was performed.

**Observed result:** inbox active time fell from 64.927 to 3.769 ms/completion (17.23x lower). Daemon CPU fell from 24.988% to 15.836% of one core (9.153 percentage points, 36.63% relative). The two consecutive AFTER windows agree. Exact daemon launch counters did not move over 120.046 s; RSS fell during that interval.

## Paired AFTER readings

The first edge was more than three minutes after daemon start, beyond a complete 55 s request lifetime and an additional 60 s settling wait. All three edges retained the same PID, build commit and process-start identity.

| UTC, November 21 | Load average 1/5/15 min | Cumulative CPU, s | RSS, KiB | Inbox ok/refused | Inbox active_us | Total daemon spawns |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 06:10:13.305289 | 35.378 / 45.055 / 64.895 | 55.33 | 134336 | 244 / 0 | 2412942 | 676 |
| 06:11:13.326945 | 23.614 / 39.743 / 61.545 | 65.14 | 134352 | 323 / 0 | 2683222 | 676 |
| 06:12:13.349132 | 39.000 / 40.592 / 60.339 | 74.34 | 118624 | 402 / 0 | 3008481 | 676 |

The host has 16 logical CPUs. Machine load remained elevated despite the settling wait; these are quiet-inbox windows, not an idle-machine benchmark.

| Window | Ping interval, s | Completions | Active delta, us | Active/completion, ms | Active/second, ms | CPU delta, s | CPU, % one core |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| First | 60.023757 | 79 | 270280 | 3.421 | 4.503 | 9.81 | 16.344 |
| Second | 60.022232 | 79 | 325259 | 4.117 | 5.419 | 9.20 | 15.328 |
| Combined | 120.045989 | 158 | 595539 | 3.769 | 4.961 | 19.01 | 15.836 |

CPU intervals from the ps edges were 60.021516, 60.022049 and 120.043565 s. Inbox refusals were zero. Every spawn-site delta was zero, reconciling to the zero total delta. RSS went 134336 -> 134352 -> 118624 KiB; this short trend is not a leak test.

Commands: `pij-rs --json ping` and `/bin/ps -p 31125 -o time=,rss=,lstart=,comm=`, at three edges 60 s apart; `os.getloadavg()` at every edge. Calculations use monotonic elapsed time and cumulative counter differences, not lifetime ps %cpu.

## BEFORE comparison and limits

Historical BEFORE was PID 22838 at 653f90ef96, November 21, 04:55:09.077-04:56:09.108 UTC: 141 successful inbox completions in 60.030824 s, 9154765 active_us, 64.927 ms/completion, 152.501 active ms/s, 15.00 CPU seconds over 60.027686 s, 24.988% core, RSS 116576 -> 121840 KiB, and 14 exact daemon launches.

Observed active/second is 30.74x lower AFTER. The health view listed 81 live Copilot seats BEFORE and 82 at every AFTER edge; these are cohort counts, not measured waiter counts. BEFORE included a spawn, two adopts, one output and 16 sends. AFTER had no register/adopt/spawn or inbox-ack completion in the measurement interval; it had 1088 whoami, 20 cards, 474 heartbeats, 23 activity calls, 11 FYI claims and nine shim sends.

Mean held time/completion was 30.254 s BEFORE versus 54.999 s AFTER, so request/activity mixes differ. BEFORE load was not recorded, and the old daemon was much older. The deployed code also contains an intervening governance change. These are measured before/after differences consistent with A1's loop reduction, not a controlled claim assigning every saved CPU second or the entire timing ratio exclusively to #310.

**Passes/completion are not measured.** The deployed `ping` route entry exposes ok, refused, active_us and held_us, not inner claim passes. The four undisturbed passes per 55 s request and six recipient reads per 20 s remain exact-head source/CI bounds. Completion counts must not be relabeled as passes.

## Separate machine and event samples

`just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json` ran only after both CPU windows, approximately 06:13:41-06:14:01 UTC: 369.0 total new processes/s, 349.4 sampled/s (lower bound), with no observed daemon child. Load 1/5/15 was 114.417/61.867/66.357 before that sampler and 97.892/61.592/66.159 after. Historical machine BEFORE was 388.7 total/s and 365.7 sampled/s. These unmatched machine windows do not establish an A1 launch reduction; A1 adds no launch site.

A concurrent bounded read-only spine range, 06:10:13.945-06:11:13.957 UTC, observed seq 4694254 -> 4694274: 20 events in 60.011100 s (0.3333/s), 2343 payload bytes, including four delivery.outcome events. No message bodies were read. At 82 waiters this would imply approximately 27.33 broadcast receives/s, not measured subscriber polls or CPU. Filtering remains inside HeldSpan; inbox active_us alone cannot price that CPU or prove fan-out dominates.

## Preservation and holding

The native AFTER measurements and comparison are preserved in this governed output. Local raw artifacts are pr310-after.ndjson, pr310-after-spawn-rate.json, pr310-after-event-rate.json and the historical pr310-before.json; the tables above preserve the public values needed to recompute the central deltas.

The authoritative performance/310 holder row for pij-golden-ant already ended at 06:07:04.408 UTC through merge delivery, before the AFTER request. It was not reassigned merely to manufacture another release. This after-deploy note is by the original reviewer. The measurement assignment is finished and the seat can be closed.
